question.prompt: \(\theta\) is between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\), inclusive, and \(\cos\theta=1\). Find \(\sin\theta\).

solutions.explanation: In this range, \(\cos\theta=1\) only when \(\theta=0^\circ\), and the sine is 0.
solutions.title: Identify the endpoint angle

solutions.explanation:
The square-sum identity lets us find sine without first finding the angle. Since \(\cos\theta=1\),
\[\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta=1-1^2=0.\]
The only real number whose square is zero is zero, so \(\sin\theta=0\).
solutions.title: Use the square-sum identity
